newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian shilling up as money flows in from Kenya.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian shilling up as money flows in from Kenya.

text.p: The Tanzanian shilling strengthened against the dollar and pound on Thursday as investors pulled dollars out of Kenya and put them into Tanzania.
The Kenyan shilling fell to an official record low against the dollar on Thursday.

The central Bank of Tanzania said the shilling exchanged at a commercial mean rate of 620.3934 versus the dollar compared to Wednesday's 621.0468. Against the pound, the shilling stood at 994.7707 from Wednesday's 1009.2042.
"For reasons we don't fully know, but involving flight capital from Kenya, the forex market is witnessing unprecedented supply," said a senior financial analyst, who declined to be identified.
"There's no question about capital flight. The Asian community in Kenya have well-established links here. Some of the Kenyan banks are sending their money to Dar es Salaam," the analyst said.
Dealers said the Bank of Tanzania (BoT) bought $10 million of Tanzanian shillings to limit the unit's gains.

"If left to private buyers, there would be a surplus of dollars chasing the same amount of shillings, which means the dollar price of shillings would rise. This is a managed float by the BoT," said a financial analyst.
A dealer from a major foreign bank said other factors also boosted the Tanzanian shilling.
"There's been a tightening in shilling liquidity. We're seeing a lot of exporters bringing dollars and exchanging to shillings to pay farmers for their crops," she said.

Other contributing factors include rising yields on BoT-issued treasury bills, which are proving popular with local investors. The BoT also recently introduced repurchase agreements (repos) to soak up surplus shillings.
